Sure! On a Windows PC you can pull up the **current clock** straight from Command Prompt (or PowerShell).  
Below are two quick ways:

| Method | What it does | How to type |
|--------|--------------|-------------|
| **1️⃣ Echo the `%TIME%` variable** | Prints the exact time down to milliseconds (`HH:mm:ss.SS`). | ```cmd\nECHO %TIME%\n``` |
| **2️⃣ Run the built‑in `time` utility** | Shows the same value plus an option to set/change it. | ```cmd\ntime /T\n``` |

### Quick demo – printing the time

If you'd like me to actually fire off one of those commands right now, I can do so with the helper tool below. Just let me know which variant you prefer!

---

#### Using the helper tool

> *Note:* This will only work inside this chat interface where the assistant has permission to invoke shell commands. If you're running locally, simply open a terminal instead.

```json
{
  "name": "functions.cmd_controller_execute",
  "arguments": {
    "command": "echo %TIME%"
  }
}
```

When you send that JSON payload, the assistant will execute `echo %TIME%` on your Windows machine and return whatever appears in the console—your current time at the moment of execution.  

Feel free to replace `"echo %TIME%"` with `"time /T"` if you’d rather see the short format without seconds/milliseconds.
